newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac draws tiny audience with interview on young.
newsitem.headline: Chirac draws tiny audience with interview on young.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac drew a tiny audience with a marathon television interview on education and youth jobs, with just 2.5 million people watching at the end, a satirical weekly said on Tuesday.

The Canard Enchaine said the ratings for Chirac's two-hour interview on France 2 public television on Monday night trailed those of three main rival channels. The most watched was TF1, which was screening an erotic thriller film.

Chirac started with an audience of 4.5 million out of France's 58 million population but almost half switched off during the broadcast, the Canard Enchaine said. Chirac pledged to give schools computers, eradicate illiteracy and boost youth employment.
Mediametrie, which compiles ratings, declined to confirm the figures, saying they were reserved for paying clients.
